angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,064,421 km at 413.93 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 2.4159 +/- 0.0253 mas (same row, RUWE 1.36): 413.93 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.53 +/- 0.14 solar radii from Boisse et al. 2013, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of HAT-P-42 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013A&A...558A..86B/abstract): 1,064,421 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.178 +/- 0.068 solar masses from Boisse et al. 2013, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of HAT-P-42 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013A&A...558A..86B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5743 +/- 50 K from Boisse et al. 2013, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HAT-P-42 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013A&A...558A..86B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Boisse et al. 2013, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of HAT-P-42 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2013A&A...558A..86B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/hat-p-42.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.140, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
